lines.text: Ben-hadad king of Aram besieged Samaria, and a donkey's head sold for eighty shekels of silver.
The king tore his clothes, then swore Elisha son of Shaphat's head would not stay on his shoulders.
Four men with leprosy decided to go to the enemy camp, and they set out at dawn.
The scouts took two chariots and followed the Arameans to the Euphrates, finding clothing and equipment along the way.
The people plundered the camp, flour and barley sold for a shekel, and they trampled the officer.
